title: Flag 6 Native Infinity Implementation Prompt Tree
description: Prompt tree that generates a Rust implementation of Flag 6 stated with native infinity: existence of a tempered positive measure μ on ℝ whose pure-point support is exactly the set of all non-trivial zeros of Ξ and whose absolutely continuous part vanishes. The implementation constructs approximations, certificates, and verification infrastructure; it does not claim to have proved existence.
flag6_native_statement: There exists a tempered positive measure μ on ℝ such that (1) the support of the pure-point part of μ is exactly {Im ρ : Ξ(ρ)=0, Re ρ = 1/2} and (2) the absolutely continuous part of μ is the zero measure.
honesty_boundary: Infinity is native (set-theoretic). The Rust code realises finite and constructive approximations, spectral data structures, and certificate traits. A completed proof of existence remains an open analytic problem; the generated code must never assert that Flag 6 has been captured solely by computation.

root.title: Flag 6 Native — Tempered Measure with Exact Zero Support and Vanishing Residual
root.prompt: Implement a Rust crate that realises the native form of Flag 6. Core obligation: provide data structures and algorithms for tempered measures on ℝ, a representation of the non-trivial zeros of Ξ, pure-point support matching, residual (absolutely continuous) mass measurement, and certificate traits that would, if discharged, constitute a proof of existence of the required measure μ. All computational work produces approximations or finite certificates; the existence claim itself stays open until an analytic proof is supplied.

children.title: Tempered Measure Data Structures
children.prompt:
Define a trait TemperedMeasure with methods:
- total_mass_against_weight(weight: fn(f64)->f64) -> f64  (for weight 1/(1+t²))
- pure_point_part() -> PurePointSpectrum
- absolutely_continuous_density() -> Option<ContinuousDensity>
- is_tempered() -> bool

Provide at least two concrete implementations:
1. AtomicMeasure — finite or countable supported pure-point measure (for approximations).
2. MixedMeasure — pure-point plus an absolutely continuous density given by a numerical function or spline.

All measures must enforce the temperedness condition ∫ d|μ|(t)/(1+t²) < ∞.

children.title: PurePointSpectrum
children.prompt: Struct PurePointSpectrum { locations: Vec<f64>, masses: Vec<f64> }. Methods: support(), total_mass(), truncate_to_height(T: f64), distance_to_known_zeros(known: &[f64]) -> f64. Locations are interpreted as imaginary parts on the critical line.

children.title: ContinuousDensity / Residual
children.prompt: Trait or struct for an absolutely continuous density ρ(t). Method residual_mass(weight) -> f64. A density is considered vanishing when residual_mass is below a configurable numerical tolerance for practical checks; exact vanishing is a mathematical statement, not a floating-point one.

children.title: Non-Trivial Zeros of Ξ
children.prompt:
Provide a ZeroOracle trait:
- known_zeros_up_to(height: f64) -> Vec<f64>  (imaginary parts of known non-trivial zeros)
- is_known_zero(im: f64, tol: f64) -> bool

Implement a concrete oracle that can load tabulated zeros (e.g. from a file or a well-known dataset of the first N zeros of ζ/Ξ) and, optionally, call an external high-precision zeta routine for verification. The oracle represents the infinite set only by finite initial segments; the full set remains an analytic object.

children.title: XiFunction Interface
children.prompt: Minimal interface to the completed xi-function Ξ(s) sufficient to evaluate or verify zeros on the critical line. Use an external library or a placeholder that documents the required analytic properties (functional equation, entire function of order 1, etc.).

children.title: Pure-Point Support Matching
children.prompt:
Implement a function match_pure_point_support(μ: &impl TemperedMeasure, oracle: &impl ZeroOracle, height: f64) -> SupportMatchReport that:
- extracts the pure-point locations of μ up to the given height,
- compares them with the known zeros up to that height,
- reports Hausdorff distance, missing zeros, and spurious locations.

Exact equality of supports on the whole line is the infinite statement; the implementation only ever checks finite height truncations.

children.title: Residual Vanishing Checks
children.prompt: Implement residual_vanishes(μ: &impl TemperedMeasure, tol: f64) -> bool for numerical checks, and a trait ExactResidualVanishing { fn residual_is_identically_zero(&self) -> Certificate; } where Certificate is an enum { Proven, NumericalEvidence{tol}, Unknown }. Only Proven corresponds to the mathematical claim in Flag 6; the other variants are computational.

children.title: Candidate Measure Construction
children.prompt:
Provide constructors that build candidate tempered measures from:
- the first K known zeros (atomic pure-point measure),
- finite-rank spectral measures coming from the geometric kernels / helix / Φ approximations already present in the framework,
- any future operator whose eigenvalues are conjectured to track the zeros.

Each constructor returns a MixedMeasure or AtomicMeasure together with a provenance record (which zeros, which truncation parameters). These are the concrete objects on which support matching and residual checks are run.

children.title: Lift from Finite Φ / Helix Models
children.prompt: Bridge the earlier CNF / helix machinery: convert a Cadical model of Φ^⋆_{N,M,K} or a helical digit string into an AtomicMeasure whose pure-point locations are the realised zeros and whose residual mass is taken from the residual variables of the model. This supplies a steady stream of candidate measures from the finitary side.

children.title: Existence Certificates (Native Flag 6)
Hooks for Analytic Input
children.prompt: Provide clear extension points (traits or callback registrations) where an external analytic argument—uniform Mourre estimate, tightness + compactness, continuity of the residual extraction step of T, or a Lyapunov functional—can be attached and thereby upgrade a Numerical/FiniteHeight certificate to Analytic. These hooks are the only route by which Flag 6 can be captured inside the crate.

children.title: Flag 6 Native Orchestrator
children.prompt:
Implement Flag6NativeOrchestrator that:
1. loads or constructs candidate measures (from known zeros, from Φ/helix models, from operator approximations),
2. runs support matching up to configurable heights,
3. runs residual vanishing checks,
4. queries any registered Flag6Certificate,
5. emits a structured report stating:
   - which finite approximations succeed,
   - whether any Analytic certificate is present,
   - that the existence of μ with the exact properties of Flag 6 remains open unless an Analytic certificate has been supplied.

Never print a claim that the Riemann Hypothesis is proved unless both SupportProof and ResidualProof are Analytic.

children.title: Documentation of Native Infinity Boundary
children.prompt:
In crate-level documentation state:

Flag 6 (native) = existence of a tempered measure μ on ℝ whose pure-point support is exactly the infinite set of non-trivial zeros of Ξ and whose residual continuous part is identically zero.

Infinity is a first-class object of the ambient set theory. The Rust implementation only ever manipulates finite approximations, numerical certificates, and hooks for analytic proofs. Capturing Flag 6 requires discharging the Analytic variants of SupportProof and ResidualProof; computation alone cannot do so.

This boundary must remain visible to every user of the crate.
